# xrpl-muse-skill

> Keyless XRPL research and safety for any agent with a terminal.
> Trading is second, behind proposing a transaction and a human
> approving the exact hash. Fresh installs are read-only until someone
> types `go live`. MIT licensed.

Repo: https://github.com/terramike/xrpl-muse-skill
HOL Guard profile: https://hol.org/guard/extensions/command.xrpl-muse-skill

## Entry points

- `README.md` — install, quick start, command map, what's new
- `SKILL.md` — safety rules, the ceremony, and pointers into `references/`
- `SECURITY.md` — the safety model and its limits
- HOL Guard profile — published command-coverage listing for the proposal,
  signing, gate-transition, and read-only command classes
- `AGENTS.md` — contributor guidance: tests, conventions, what never
  to touch
- `references/` — deep docs per topic: `onboarding-wizard.md`,
  `ecosystem-connectors.md`, `trusted-links.md` (curated links with dates),
  `farm.md` (Farmers Union explainer + link bundle),
  `commands.md`, `menu-presentation.md`
- `bin/xrpl-trade` — keyless reads and proposal builds; does not submit
- `bin/xrpl-sign` — signs a proposal only with `--approve` of the exact hash, and refuses while read-only
- `bin/xrpl_eco.py` — ecosystem read modules (validators, amendments,
  stablecoin, oracle)

## Safety invariants (do not work around these)

1. Fresh installs are read-only. `xrpl-trade live` requires typing
   `go live` at an interactive prompt — there is deliberately no CLI
   flag or env var to skip it.
2. The propose path does not read a seed and does not submit.
   `xrpl-sign` signs only with `--approve` of the exact hash and refuses
   while read-only. Opt-in commands in `xrpl-trade` can store a seed.
   `wallet backup` and autopilot's backup ceremony can display a seed once.
3. Do not paste a seed into chat. A backup that prints a seed on the
   operator's terminal puts that seed in the transcript.
4. Network reads fail open (clear "unavailable", never fabricated data);
   external data is always attributed, never presented as ledger truth.

## Quick commands (all keyless reads)

```bash
xrpl-trade validators        # signed validator-list health
xrpl-trade amendments         # amendment votes + majority countdown
xrpl-trade stablecoin RLUSD   # supply by chain + price
xrpl-trade oracle XRP USD     # on-ledger XLS-47 prices (Band + DIA)
xrpl-trade token-safety --help
xrpl-trade trace rABC... [--depth 2]         # funding-origin chain
xrpl-trade links rABC... rDEF... [--window 200]  # shared counterparties
xrpl-trade flow rABC... [--window 200]          # top counterparties by volume
xrpl-trade nft-trail 00081F...                  # NFT mint -> sale provenance
xrpl-trade token-trail --issuer r... --currency USD  # issuer + holders + issuer-involved movers
xrpl-trade <command> --help   # every command documents itself
```

Say "menu" for the button menus: XRPL Actions (Markets + 🔎 Forensics:
🧬 Trace, 🔗 Links, 🌊 Flow, 🖼️ NFT Trail, 🪙 Token Trail), NFT, Artists,
Wallets, XRP News, XRPLF, Coffee & Crypto (🎰 LuckyHash), xBoost.

Say "luckyhash menu" for the LuckyHash gaming deep links (reference only —
the assistant cannot place bets; every bet is signed in the user's wallet).
See `references/luckyhash.md`.

## Propose → approve → sign (needs human approval)

```bash
xrpl-trade buy --pair XRP/RLUSD --amount 10 --price 1.50  # proposal + hash
xrpl-sign --profile main --approve <hash>                 # human signs
```

## Tests

```bash
python3 -m unittest tests.test_readonly
python3 -m unittest tests.test_eco
```
